```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Han 2023 built a Simcyp whole-body PBPK model of the budesonide
controlled-release capsule Entocort EC in healthy volunteers and Crohn's
disease patients, and used it for virtual bioequivalence trials comparing
local gut and systemic exposure across eight virtual test formulations. The
formulation enters that PBPK model as a Weibull dissolution function fitted to
the in vitro dissolution profile of the Entocort EC pellets (Equation 4,
Table 2, Supplementary Table S1). That dissolution function is packaged here.

* Model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Han_2023_budesonide_dissolution"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Han_2023_budesonide_dissolution"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15092237>
* Supplement (Table S1): <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/pharmaceutics15092237/s1>

The PBPK model itself is not part of the package. Its tissue distribution uses
Simcyp's Rodgers and Rowland method with only a global Kp scalar (0.8)
reported, its hepatic and gut clearance is a CYP3A4 intrinsic clearance per
pmol of enzyme that needs Simcyp's enzyme abundances and organ scalars, and its
absorption runs through Simcyp's eight-segment multilayer gut wall (M-ADAM)
model with regional absorption scalars applied to internal permeabilities.
None of the organ volumes, blood flows, tissue partition coefficients or
enzyme abundances behind those inputs are printed, so the PBPK model cannot be
reproduced from the publication.

# Population

The dissolution function is an in vitro curve fit, not a population model.
The source profile is the Entocort EC pellet dissolution in fasted-state
simulated intestinal fluid (FaSSIF) reported by Effinger et al. (Eur J Pharm
Sci 2021;157:105617; Han 2023 reference 22), sampled every 0.5 h up to 6 h.
Because the measured profile had not reached 100% at its last sampling time,
the authors added a 100% point at the end of the profile (Section 2.4.4).
There is no inter-individual variability and no residual error. The same
information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Han_2023_budesonide_dissolution")()$population`.

The eight virtual test formulations of the paper were built by hand from that
reference profile. Six shift the percent dissolved by a fixed number of
percentage points at every sampling time (+20%, +10%, +5%, +3%, -5%, -10%,
capped at 100%) and were refitted to the same Weibull function (Table 2). The
other two keep the Entocort EC profile and change only the enteric-coating
trigger pH (5 or 6 instead of 5.5), which affects release in vivo but not the
in vitro dissolution curve.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Weibull dissolution, `F = Fmax * (1 - exp(-(t - Tlag)^beta / alpha))` | n/a | Equation (4) |
| `lra` (`ra = alpha^(-1/beta)`) | log(3.1196^(-1/0.93998)) = log(0.298) 1/h | Table S1 (Alpha = 3.1196, Beta = 0.93998); Table 2 (alpha = 3.12) |
| `lgam1` (`beta`) | log(0.93998) | Table S1 (Beta = 0.93998); Table 2 (beta = 0.94) |
| `lfdepot` (`Fmax / 100`) | log(1), fixed | Table S1 and Table 2 (Fmax = 100) |
| `Tlag` | 0 | not reported; see Assumptions |
| Virtual formulations (alpha, beta) | +20% (1.53, 0.87); +10% (2.14, 0.89); +5% (2.56, 0.91); +3% (2.77, 0.92); -5% (3.90, 1.01); -10% (5.01, 1.09) | Table 2 |
| Similarity factor `f2` | Equation (3) | Section 2.4.4 |
| Residual error, inter-individual variability | none | deterministic curve fit |

The canonical Weibull release input in nlmixr2lib leaves the fraction still
undissolved as `S(t) = exp(-(ra * t)^gam1)`. Matching it to Equation (4)
gives `gam1 = beta` and `ra = alpha^(-1/beta)`, so the `lra` value is computed
from the published `alpha` and `beta`, not printed directly.

# Simulation

One 3 mg Entocort EC capsule is dosed into `depot` at the start of
dissolution, and the dissolved amount is read from the `released` sink. The
virtual formulations reuse the same model with `lra` and `lgam1` overridden by
the Table 2 values.

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Han_2023_budesonide_dissolution"))

dose_mg <- 3
# Rounded so the 0.5 h sampling times below match exactly.
obs_h <- sort(unique(round(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), 11, 12), 4)))
ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot", evid = 1L),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = obs_h, amt = 0, cmt = "released", evid = 0L)
)

# Table 2 Weibull parameters, in the alpha / beta form of Equation (4).
# Entocort EC uses the full-precision Table S1 values carried by the model.
formulations <- tibble::tribble(
  ~formulation,   ~shift, ~alpha,  ~beta,   ~f2_published,
  "Entocort EC",  0,      3.1196,  0.93998, NA,
  "+20%",         20,     1.53,    0.87,    36.1,
  "+10%",         10,     2.14,    0.89,    50.8,
  "+5%",          5,      2.56,    0.91,    65.5,
  "+3%",          3,      2.77,    0.92,    75.8,
  "-5%",          -5,     3.90,    1.01,    65.5,
  "-10%",         -10,    5.01,    1.09,    50.8
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(formulation = factor(formulation, levels = formulation))

solve_formulation <- function(alpha, beta) {
  sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod,
    events = ev,
    params = c(lra = log(alpha^(-1 / beta)), lgam1 = log(beta)),
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12
  )
  as.data.frame(sim) |>
    dplyr::transmute(time, released, releaseRate, pct = 100 * released / dose_mg)
}

sim <- formulations |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(formulation, shift, alpha, beta, solve_formulation(alpha, beta))
```

## Check against the published closed form

The ODE solution must reproduce Equation (4) evaluated at the published
parameters. Both sides use the same values, so the only difference is
integration error and a tight bound is appropriate.

```{r closed-form}
weibull_pct <- function(t, alpha, beta) 100 * (1 - exp(-t^beta / alpha))

cf <- sim |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_closed = weibull_pct(time, alpha, beta), diff = pct - pct_closed)

cf |>
  dplyr::group_by(formulation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(max_abs_diff = max(abs(diff))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Formulation" = formulation, "Max |ODE - Equation (4)| (points)" = max_abs_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 6)

stopifnot(max(abs(cf$diff)) < 0.01)
```

The model dissolves the whole capsule: at 24 h the undissolved fraction of
the Entocort EC profile is `r signif(exp(-24^0.93998 / 3.1196), 2)`, so
`tad()` restarting at a second daily capsule does not lose drug from the
first.

# Replicate Figure 2

The points below were digitised by the maintainers from the thick blue
reference profile of Figure 2 (sampling times 0.5 to 6 h, with the 100% end
point). The lines are the packaged Weibull model at the Table 2 parameters.

```{r digitised}
# Entocort EC reference profile, digitised from Han 2023 Figure 2 (percent
# dissolved). The final point is the 100% assumed by the authors; the figure
# draws it at 11 h while Section 2.4.4 says 12 h.
ref_digitised <- data.frame(
  time = c(seq(0.5, 6, by = 0.5), 12),
  pct = c(14.8, 28.6, 38.8, 47.0, 53.3, 59.1, 64.3, 68.8, 72.4, 76.4, 79.5, 84.4, 100)
)
```

```{r figure2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
ggplot(sim, aes(time, pct, colour = formulation, linetype = shift < 0)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(
    data = ref_digitised, aes(time, pct), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "black", size = 1.8
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "dashed"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 12), ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Dissolved (%)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Weibull dissolution of Entocort EC and virtual formulations",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Han 2023. Points: Entocort EC profile digitised from Figure 2."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Known-answer checks

The packaged curve, the digitised data and the published table are tied
together in three ways. All three are deterministic.

1. **The packaged Entocort EC curve passes through the digitised reference
   profile.** Digitising error is about one percentage point. The bound
   applies to the twelve measured points (0.5 to 6 h). The 100% end point was
   added by the authors rather than measured, and the fitted Weibull reaches
   only about 96% at 12 h, so it is shown in the table but not bounded.

```{r check-reference}
sampling_h <- c(seq(0.5, 6, by = 0.5), 12)
ref_model <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(formulation == "Entocort EC", round(time, 4) %in% sampling_h) |>
  dplyr::transmute(time = round(time, 4), pct_model = pct)
chk_ref <- dplyr::inner_join(ref_digitised, ref_model, by = "time") |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = pct_model - pct)

chk_ref |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time (h)" = time, "Digitised (%)" = pct,
    "Model (%)" = pct_model, "Model - digitised (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

measured <- chk_ref$time <= 6
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk_ref) == length(sampling_h),
  median(abs(chk_ref$diff[measured])) < 1.5,
  max(abs(chk_ref$diff[measured])) < 3,
  abs(chk_ref$diff[!measured] + 3.6) < 0.5
)
```

2. **Refitting Equation (4) to the digitised profile recovers the published
   alpha and beta.** This also settles the form of the Weibull: with `alpha`
   dividing `t^beta`, as printed, the refit lands on the Table S1 values;
   reading `alpha` as a time scale inside the power, `(t / alpha)^beta`, would
   need `alpha` near 3.3 instead.

```{r check-refit}
refit <- stats::nls(
  pct ~ 100 * (1 - exp(-time^beta / alpha)),
  data = ref_digitised,
  start = list(alpha = 3, beta = 1)
)
refit_coef <- stats::coef(refit)
data.frame(
  parameter = c("alpha", "beta"),
  published = c(3.1196, 0.93998),
  refit_to_digitised = unname(refit_coef[c("alpha", "beta")])
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = refit_to_digitised / published) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = parameter, "Table S1" = published,
    "Refit to digitised Figure 2" = refit_to_digitised, "Ratio" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(abs(refit_coef[["alpha"]] / 3.1196 - 1) < 0.03, abs(refit_coef[["beta"]] / 0.93998 - 1) < 0.03)
```

3. **The similarity factors of Table 2 follow from the virtual profiles.**
   Equation (3) applied to the digitised reference and the shifted profiles
   (reference plus the shift at each of the twelve measured sampling times,
   capped at 100%, and the same 100% end point as the reference)
   must reproduce the published f2 values; applied to the packaged Weibull
   curves of each virtual formulation it must land close to them, which tests
   the Table 2 `alpha` / `beta` pairs. The mean shift of each Weibull curve over
   0.5 to 6 h must also match the formulation's nominal shift.

```{r check-f2}
f2 <- function(r, t) 50 * log10(100 / sqrt(1 + mean((r - t)^2)))

model_at <- function(form) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::filter(formulation == form, round(time, 4) %in% sampling_h) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time) |>
    dplyr::pull(pct)
}
ref_curve <- model_at("Entocort EC")

chk_f2 <- formulations |>
  dplyr::filter(formulation != "Entocort EC") |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    f2_digitised = f2(ref_digitised$pct, pmin(c(ref_digitised$pct[1:12] + shift, 100), 100)),
    f2_weibull = f2(ref_curve, model_at(as.character(formulation))),
    mean_shift_weibull = mean(model_at(as.character(formulation))[1:12] - ref_curve[1:12])
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

chk_f2 |>
  dplyr::select(formulation, shift, f2_published, f2_digitised, f2_weibull, mean_shift_weibull) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Formulation" = formulation, "Nominal shift (points)" = shift,
    "f2, Table 2" = f2_published, "f2, digitised profiles" = f2_digitised,
    "f2, packaged Weibull curves" = f2_weibull,
    "Mean Weibull shift, 0.5-6 h (points)" = mean_shift_weibull
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(chk_f2$f2_digitised - chk_f2$f2_published) < 0.3),
  all(abs(chk_f2$f2_weibull - chk_f2$f2_published) < 2.5),
  all(abs(chk_f2$mean_shift_weibull - chk_f2$shift) < 1.5)
)
```

The f2 values computed from the Weibull curves sit within about 1.6 units of
Table 2, as expected for a three-parameter fit to a hand-shifted profile; the
digitised profiles reproduce Table 2 to the printed precision.

# Dissolution milestones

The paper does not tabulate dissolution times, so these are reported for
reference only, from the closed-form inverse of Equation (4):
`t_p = (-alpha * log(1 - p))^(1/beta)`.

```{r milestones}
milestones <- formulations |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    t50 = (-alpha * log(1 - 0.5))^(1 / beta),
    t632 = alpha^(1 / beta),
    t80 = (-alpha * log(1 - 0.8))^(1 / beta),
    t90 = (-alpha * log(1 - 0.9))^(1 / beta)
  )
milestones |>
  dplyr::select(formulation, alpha, beta, t50, t632, t80, t90) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Formulation" = formulation, "alpha" = alpha, "beta" = beta,
    "t50% (h)" = t50, "t63.2% (h)" = t632, "t80% (h)" = t80, "t90% (h)" = t90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Noncompartmental analysis

Not applicable. The model has no disposition, so there is no concentration
profile to analyse with PKNCA; the paper's plasma and gut-segment Cmax and AUC
values (Tables 6 and 7) are outputs of the Simcyp PBPK model, which is not
packaged. The validation above uses the dissolution profile the function was
fitted to and the similarity factors derived from it.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PBPK model not packaged.** Only the formulation input (the Weibull
  dissolution function) is extracted. The whole-body PBPK model, the Crohn's
  disease population changes (Table 4), the within-subject variability of the
  virtual bioequivalence trials (Table 5) and the bioequivalence heatmaps are
  Simcyp platform constructs whose organ-level parameters the paper does not
  print.
* **Weibull form.** Equation (4) divides `(t - Tlag)^beta` by `alpha`, which is
  Simcyp's Weibull dissolution form. The refit of the digitised Figure 2
  profile above confirms that reading.
* **Lag time.** Equation (4) includes `Tlag`, but no value is reported for any
  formulation. It is taken as zero, which the published `alpha` and `beta`
  require to reproduce Figure 2. In vivo, the Entocort EC coating starts to
  dissolve only above pH 5.5 (Table 2, trigger pH), after a 0.8 h mean pellet
  residence time in the stomach (Table S1); both belong to the PBPK model and
  are not represented here, so time zero of this model is the start of
  dissolution, not the time of capsule ingestion.
* **End of the profile.** Section 2.4.4 says 100% dissolution was assumed at
  12 h; Figure 2 draws the 100% point at about 11 h. The f2 values do not
  depend on that time, and the checks above use 12 h.
* **Precision.** The model uses the five-figure Table S1 values for Entocort
  EC; Table 2 prints the same fit rounded to `alpha = 3.12`, `beta = 0.94`.
  The virtual formulations are available only at the Table 2 precision.
* **Figure 2 legend.** The legend prints f2 = 65.6 for the +5% formulation
  (Table 2: 65.5) and "f2+50.8" for -10%; the Table 2 values are used.
* **Trigger-pH formulations.** The "pH threshold = 5" and "pH threshold = 6"
  formulations have the Entocort EC Weibull parameters and differ only in the
  in vivo trigger pH, so their in vitro dissolution curve is the reference
  curve.
